title: Point perfectness of global sections
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum and the coefficient stages
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ of the Poincare duality
conventions [def-pod-conventions], but let $X_0$ be an arbitrary
separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme: neither properness nor smoothness
of $X_0$ is assumed. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$a_X:X\to s=\Spec k$ be the structure morphism, and let
$d\geq\dim X$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda )$. Then the four
complexes

$$
R\Gamma (X,K),\qquad R\Gamma _c(X,K),\qquad R\Gamma (X,K)^\vee,\qquad R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee
$$

are perfect point complexes at every coefficient stage, in the
following sense.

1. At finite level $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ they are bounded with finite
cohomology modules and finite Tor amplitude, i.e. quasi-isomorphic to
bounded complexes of finite free $A$-modules
([def-pod-perfect-point-complex]). If $K$ has Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$, then $R\Gamma(X,K)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ have Tor amplitude
in $[a,b+2d]$ and their duals in $[-b-2d,-a]$.
1. At the stage $\mathcal O_E$ they lie in
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ and are perfect; their reductions
modulo $\varpi_E^n$ are the corresponding finite-level complexes of the
reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, and these are
perfect with one common amplitude independent of $n$.
1. At the stages $E$ and $\Qlb$ they are bounded with
finite-dimensional cohomology.

If $X_0$ is proper, the canonical comparison
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,K)$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] identifies the two cases; in
particular this applies in the fixed setting of
[def-pod-conventions]. (Source: the finiteness theorems of etale
cohomology, Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Sections 19 and 29,
for the finiteness and the perfectness at the point. The finite-level
compact-support membership $R\Gamma _c(X,K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$
is recorded in [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness].)

proof.text: The base change $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ is separated and of finite type over $k$ by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. All coefficients below are those of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]; in particular $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is finite local, and $R=\mathcal O_E$ is a discrete valuation ring. We use $R\Gamma=\operatorname{Fib}_sRa_{X,*}$ and $R\Gamma_c=\operatorname{Fib}_sRa_{X,!}$ as defined in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], with the intrinsic finite-Tor categories of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. If $X$ is empty, the empty covering forces every module sheaf on $X$ to be zero. Thus $K$, its two direct images, their point complexes, and their duals are zero. They satisfy every requested vanishing bound, including when $d<0$. Henceforth $X$ is nonempty; then its Krull dimension is nonnegative, so $d\geq0$. No smoothness, geometric connectedness, or exceptional-adjoint admissibility from [def-pod-conventions] is used: only its coefficient notation is retained.

source.place: Proof, opening of Step 1 and the arbitrary separated finite-type hypotheses

proof.text: Here is the point passage used at finite level. If $N\in D^b_c(s_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ has Tor amplitude $[u,v]$, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives $N\simeq\nu_s^*N_{\mathrm{et}}$, and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) gives the same Tor interval for $N_{\mathrm{et}}$. Apply [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] with the separable closure of the algebraically closed field $k$ equal to $k$ itself: its Galois group is trivial, so the stalk functor identifies abelian sheaves on $s_{\mathrm{et}}$ with abelian groups. This identifies $A_n$-module sheaves with $A_n$-modules by carrying the scalar action maps along the equivalence. It is exact, and is compatible with module tensor products by [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar](1). Consequently it identifies derived tensor products, computed by flat resolutions, and takes the Tor interval of $N_{\mathrm{et}}$ to the ordinary-module Tor interval $[u,v]$. The comparison of global cohomology [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] identifies this module complex with $\operatorname{Fib}_sN=\Gamma(s,N)$: pro-étale sections at $s$ are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], and on the étale side sections are the stalk under the preceding trivial-Galois equivalence. Finally [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness](1) says that this complex is bounded with finite cohomology. This argument concerns constructible objects of étale origin; it makes no claim that all pro-étale sheaves on $s$ are constant.

source.place: Proof, Step 1, passage from a constructible object at the geometric point to a module complex

proof.text: At finite level let $K$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] to $a_X:X\to s$, which has exactly the separated finite-type hypotheses and source-dimension bound $\dim X\leq d$ in that statement. It gives $Ra_{X,*}K\in D^b_c(s,A_n)$ with Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$. The point passage in Step 2 therefore proves that $R\Gamma(X,K)$ is bounded with finite cohomology and ordinary-module Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$.

Choose a scheme-theoretically dense compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{p}s$ by [det-nagata-theorem-dense]; $s$ is affine and hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The scheme $\bar X$ is finite type over $k$ (since $p$ is proper), and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. We justify the dimension bound rather than assuming it for an arbitrary compactification. Scheme-theoretic density implies topological density: a nonempty open disjoint from $X$ would have its nonzero structure sheaf inject into zero. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], $\bar X$ has finitely many irreducible components $Z_i$. For each $i$, maximality of the finitely many distinct components makes $\bar X\setminus\bigcup_{h\ne i}Z_h$ a nonempty open contained in $Z_i$. Density of the open $X$ makes its intersection with this open nonempty. Hence every $Z_i\cap X$ is nonempty open in $Z_i$. Give $Z_i$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is an irreducible finite-type $k$-scheme (on affine charts its ring is a quotient of a finite-type $k$-algebra), and [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] gives $\dim Z_i=\dim(Z_i\cap X)\leq\dim X$. The inequalities and $\dim\bar X=\max_i\dim Z_i$ follow directly from chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]: each such chain lies in a component, and intersection of a chain in a closed subset with its ambient space preserves it. Thus $\dim\bar X\leq d$.

source.place: Proof, Step 1, compactification and the bound on its dimension

proof.text: By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], $K$ has an étale-origin witness, so the compactification construction [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] applies to it; for this étale-origin object the comparison through a common refinement of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] identifies the functor attached to any chosen compactification with the one attached to $(j,p)$, giving $Ra_{X,!}K\simeq Rp_*j_!K$. By [lem-trf-open-ctf], $j_!K$ is bounded constructible with precisely the same allowed Tor interval $[a,b]$. Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] to the proper morphism $p$ and the dimension bound proved in Step 4. It gives $Rp_*j_!K\in D^b_c(s,A_n)$ with Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$. Step 2 now gives boundedness, finite cohomology and this ordinary-module Tor interval for $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$. In particular no compact-support projection formula on arbitrary unbounded coefficients is needed here.

Let $C$ be either finite-level complex just obtained, and put $[u,v]=[a,b+2d]$. First [lem-trf-finite-tor-amplitude-perfect] supplies a bounded finite free complex representing $C$. Regard that particular complex as a bounded complex of finitely generated modules over the Noetherian local ring $A_n$ (Noetherianity also follows immediately since the ring is finite). Now [lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect] applies to this representative and its established ordinary-module Tor interval, giving a finite free representative $P^\bullet$ with $P^i=0$ outside $[u,v]$. This second citation is necessary: the first citation alone does not assert a degree bound. By [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom], with target $A_n[0]$, the derived dual is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}^\bullet(P^\bullet,A_n)$, whose degree $i$ term is $\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(P^{-i},A_n)$ and whose differential is the signed transpose. These terms are finite free, and vanish outside $[-v,-u]$. Tensoring this bounded free complex with any module computes its derived tensor and has no terms outside that interval, so the dual has the asserted Tor amplitude. Its cohomology is finite, being subquotients of finite modules. This proves all finite-level assertions and the perfectness of all four objects in [def-pod-perfect-point-complex].

source.place: Proof, Step 1, finite free models and duals

proof.text: At the integral stage put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $K_n=K\otimes_R^LA_n$. The integral hypothesis $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$ supplies a single Tor interval $[a,b]$ for all $K_n$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; their bounded constructibility and derived completeness of $K$ are those of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Apply [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] to $a_X$: it states both $Ra_{X,*}K\in D^b_c(s,R)$ and the canonical isomorphisms $(Ra_{X,*}K)\otimes_R^LA_n\simeq Ra_{X,*,n}K_n$. Apply [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] to the same morphism, the nonnegative bound $d$, and the common interval $[a,b]$: it states $Ra_{X,!}K\in D^b_c(s,R)$ and the analogous canonical compact-support comparisons. Applying sections and [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] makes these comparisons isomorphisms of ordinary $A_n$-module complexes. Thus, for either $C=R\Gamma(X,K)$ or $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$, $C\otimes_R^LA_n$ is exactly the corresponding finite-level complex of $K_n$. By Step 6 these reductions have finite free models in $[a,b+2d]$, independent of $n$. By [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness](2), $C$ belongs to $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius] now gives that $C$ is perfect over the DVR $R$. This uses the existing algebraic perfectness theorem in place of the source's uncited derived-Nakayama and resolution arguments.

source.place: Proof, Step 2, integral direct images, finite reductions, and perfectness

proof.text: Choose a bounded finite projective $R$-complex $P^\bullet$ representing either integral complex $C$ of Step 7. The Hom-complex formula [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom], applied to $P^\bullet$ and $R[0]$, represents $C^\vee$ by the bounded complex with terms $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^{-i},R)$. These terms are finite projective: a splitting of $P^{-i}$ from a finite free module dualizes to a splitting of its dual from the dual finite free module. Thus $C^\vee$ is perfect. Since $R$ is Noetherian, each kernel of its differential is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], and its cohomology is a quotient of that kernel. Consequently the dual has bounded finitely generated cohomology.

source.place: Proof, Step 2, duals, their reductions and membership in the integral point category

proof.text: To verify completeness, apply [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2) at $s$: the completed integral coefficient unit is constructible and has the rank-one free $A_n$-units as its reductions. In particular its reductions have Tor interval $[0,0]$, so the unit assertion of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] identifies its point fibre with $R[0]$. By [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness](2) and [def-weil-point-fg-complete-complexes], that fibre is derived complete for $(\varpi_E)$. Now [lem-sf-perfect-over-derived-complete-ring], with $A=R$, $I=(\varpi_E)$, and the perfect complex $C^\vee$ of Step 8, supplies derived completeness of $C^\vee$. Together with its bounded finite cohomology, this gives $C^\vee\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ by the same point-category definition. This citation carries the retract and bounded-filtration argument; neither assertion is being inferred from a definition.

source.place: Proof, Step 2, duals, their reductions and membership in the integral point category

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect] to $R\to A_n$, with perfect first argument $C$ from Step 7 and second argument $R[0]$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $C^\vee\otimes_R^L A_n\simeq(C\otimes_R^L A_n)^\vee$. By Steps 6 and 7 these are exactly the finite-level duals, with common Tor interval $[-b-2d,-a]$. The original reductions have the common interval $[a,b+2d]$. Taking the minimum of their lower endpoints and the maximum of their upper endpoints gives an interval containing the Tor intervals of all four families, independently of $n$.

source.place: Proof, Step 2, duals, their reductions and membership in the integral point category

proof.text: For $E$-coefficients, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] says that every object is represented by an integral $K_R$; it is raw scalar localization, so no formally adjoined direct summand needs to be considered. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], the integral representative $K_R\in D^b_c(X,R)$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$: choose a bounded cohomological interval for its residue reduction; the lemma gives that same Tor interval for every reduction. Thus Step 7 applies to this representative. Here $\ell$ is invertible on $X$, since $\ell\ne p$. Ordinary direct image is rationalized as in [def-weil-derived-direct-image], compact support as in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and the point fibre as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Thus each of the two $E$-point complexes is represented by $E\otimes_RP^\bullet$, with $P^\bullet$ a bounded finite projective representative from Step 7. Every term is a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space, so all cohomology spaces are finite-dimensional and vanish outside a finite interval. By [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom], its dual is the finite-dimensional termwise dual with reversed degrees and has the same bounded-finiteness property. For $\Qlb$-coefficients every object has a finite coefficient field of definition by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; the ordinary and compact-support operations and the point fibre are the corresponding common-stage operations in the definitions just cited. Represent the input at one such field $E'$. The output point complexes are represented by their bounded finite-dimensional $E'$-complexes just proved. Extending the finite matrices and their dual matrices to $\Qlb$ yields bounded finite-dimensional complexes and their duals. This proves the field clauses without imposing a Weil structure on $K$.

source.place: Proof, Step 3, rational and algebraically closed coefficient stages

proof.text: If $X_0$ is proper, its base change $a_X$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The actual comparison $Ra_{X,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X,*}$ is [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence], not part of the definition of cohomology. Applying the point functor [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] gives the displayed canonical comparison of compact and ordinary point complexes; applying derived duality also identifies their duals. The same statement covers every coefficient stage, so the preceding descriptions refer to the same complexes when properness is imposed, in particular in any proper specialization of the conventions.

proof_origin.place: Proof, Steps 1–4, with all uncited point/algebraic arguments replaced by the explicit steps and existing statements cited below

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the finite-field datum and the coefficient stages
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ of the Poincare duality
conventions [def-pod-conventions], but let $X_0$ be an arbitrary
separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme: neither properness nor smoothness
of $X_0$ is assumed. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$a_X:X\to s=\Spec k$ be the structure morphism, and let
$d\geq\dim X$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda )$. Then the four
complexes

$$
R\Gamma (X,K),\qquad R\Gamma _c(X,K),\qquad R\Gamma (X,K)^\vee,\qquad R\Gamma _c(X,K)^\vee
$$

are perfect point complexes at every coefficient stage, in the
following sense.

1. At finite level $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ they are bounded with finite
cohomology modules and finite Tor amplitude, i.e. quasi-isomorphic to
bounded complexes of finite free $A$-modules
([def-pod-perfect-point-complex]). If $K$ has Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$, then $R\Gamma(X,K)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ have Tor amplitude
in $[a,b+2d]$ and their duals in $[-b-2d,-a]$.
1. At the stage $\mathcal O_E$ they lie in
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ and are perfect; their reductions
modulo $\varpi_E^n$ are the corresponding finite-level complexes of the
reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, and these are
perfect with one common amplitude independent of $n$.
1. At the stages $E$ and $\Qlb$ they are bounded with
finite-dimensional cohomology.

If $X_0$ is proper, the canonical comparison
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,K)$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] identifies the two cases; in
particular this applies in the fixed setting of
[def-pod-conventions].

proof.text:
*Step 1: the finite level.* Let $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$
([def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility],
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]). At the geometric point $s$ a bounded
constructible complex is a bounded complex of $A$-modules with finite
cohomology ([def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]), and the Tor
amplitude of a complex on $s$ is the Tor amplitude of the underlying
$A$-module complex, since the sheaves of $A$-modules on $s$ are the
$A$-modules.

For ordinary cohomology, apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale]
to the separated finite-type morphism $a_X:X\to s$: the complex
$Ra_{X,*}K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$. Hence $R\Gamma(X,K)$ is bounded, has finite cohomology
modules, and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$. No properness is used.

For compact support, choose a compactification $a_X=\bar a\circ j$
with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar a$ proper
([def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]); replacing $\bar X$ by
the scheme-theoretic closure of $X$ we may assume $\dim\bar X\leq d$.
Then $Ra_{X,!}K=R\bar a_*j_!K$. Extension by zero is exact and
commutes with derived tensor product, as one checks on stalks, so
$j_!K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, and
[cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] applied to $\bar a$ gives Tor
amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$ for $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$. The finiteness and
boundedness of its cohomology is
[prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness].

By [lem-trf-finite-tor-amplitude-perfect], a bounded complex of
$A$-modules with finite cohomology and Tor amplitude in $[a',b']$ is
quasi-isomorphic to a complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $A$-modules
with $P^i=0$ for $i\notin[a',b']$. Hence $R\Gamma(X,K)$ and
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ are represented by bounded complexes of finite free
$A$-modules in degrees $[a,b+2d]$. For such a $P^\bullet$ the derived
dual $P^{\bullet\vee}=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^\bullet,A)$ is computed
termwise, $P^\bullet$ being a bounded complex of projectives, and is
the complex of finite free modules $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-i},A)$
in degrees $[-b-2d,-a]$. Thus all four complexes are perfect point
complexes in the sense of [def-pod-perfect-point-complex], with the
stated amplitudes.

*Step 2: the stage $\mathcal O_E$.* Put $R=\mathcal O_E$,
$A_n=A_{E,n}$, $\kappa=A_1$, and let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ be a
derived-complete integral object
([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]) with reductions
$K_n=K\otimes^L_RA_n$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] all the
$K_n$ have Tor amplitude in one interval $[a,b]$, namely the
cohomological range of $K_1$. By Step 1 every
$R\Gamma(X,K_n)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)$ is a bounded complex of finite
free $A_n$-modules in the common interval $[a',b']=[a,b+2d]$.

For compact support, [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] applied to
$a_X$ gives $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\in D^b_c(s,R)$ with
$R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_RA_n\cong R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)$, these
reductions having the uniform Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$; the integral
compact support is the one of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

For ordinary cohomology, by [def-weil-derived-direct-image]
$R\Gamma(X,K)=R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(X,K_n)$. The coefficient
comparisons of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], applied to the
quotients $A_m\to A_n$ ($m\geq n$), are isomorphisms
$R\Gamma(X,K_m)\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,K_n)$
compatible with successive quotients, so
$(R\Gamma(X,K_n))_n$ is a normalized DVR tower on the point
([def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]).
[lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] then gives
$R\Gamma(X,K)\otimes^L_RA_n\cong R\Gamma(X,K_n)$ for all $n$, and
$R\Gamma(X,K)$ is derived complete.

It remains to see that a derived-complete $R$-complex $C$ whose
reductions $C_n=C\otimes^L_RA_n$ are perfect with amplitude in
$[a',b']$ is perfect. The triangle
$C\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}C\to C_1\to$ gives exact sequences

$$
0\to H^i(C)/\varpi_EH^i(C)\to H^i(C_1)\to H^{i+1}(C)[\varpi_E]\to0 .
$$

Each $H^i(C)$ is a derived-complete $R$-module, the cohomology modules
of a derived-complete complex being derived complete. By the derived
Nakayama lemma for the ideal $(\varpi_E)$ of the Noetherian ring $R$,
a derived-complete module $M$ with $M/\varpi_EM=0$ vanishes, and one
with $M/\varpi_EM$ finitely generated is finitely generated. Hence
$H^i(C)=0$ for $i\notin[a',b']$ and every $H^i(C)$ is a finitely
generated $R$-module, i.e. $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$. Since $R$ is
a discrete valuation ring, every finitely generated $R$-module has a
two-term resolution by finite free modules and every complex over $R$
is quasi-isomorphic to the sum of its shifted cohomology modules;
therefore $C$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite free
$R$-modules, i.e. it is perfect ([def-pod-perfect-point-complex]),
and its reductions are the perfect complexes $C_n$ of common
amplitude $[a',b']$. Applied to $C=R\Gamma(X,K)$ and
$C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ this proves the assertion for these two complexes.

For the duals, if $P^\bullet$ is a bounded complex of finite free
$R$-modules representing $C$, then $C^\vee$ is the termwise dual
complex, again bounded and finite free, and
$C^\vee\otimes^L_RA_n\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(P^\bullet\otimes_RA_n,A_n)=C_n^\vee$;
by Step 1 these reductions are perfect in the common interval
$[-b',-a']$.

*Step 3: the field stages.* For $\Lambda=E$, the object is the
rationalization of an integral object $K_R$
([def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]), possibly up to a direct
summand, and the operations $R\Gamma$ and $R\Gamma_c$ at the stage $E$
are the rationalizations of the integral ones
([def-weil-derived-direct-image],
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]). By Step 2 they
are $C\otimes_RE$ with $C$ a perfect $R$-complex; since
$R\to E$ is flat, $H^i(C\otimes_RE)=H^i(C)\otimes_RE$ is
finite-dimensional and vanishes outside the bounded interval of $C$,
and $(C\otimes_RE)^\vee=C^\vee\otimes_RE$ has the same property. A
direct summand of a bounded complex with finite-dimensional cohomology
is again one. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, the object is represented at a
finite stage $E'/\Ql$ ([def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]),
and all four complexes are obtained from the $E'$-stage complexes by
the exact extension of scalars $-\otimes_{E'}\Qlb$, which preserves
boundedness, finite-dimensionality and commutes with the dual of a
complex with finite-dimensional total cohomology. This proves the
field-stage assertions.

*Step 4: the proper case.* If $X_0$ is proper, then $a_X$ is proper
and the comparison $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\to R\Gamma(X,K)$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] is an isomorphism at each
stage, compatible with the constructions above; in the setting of
[def-pod-conventions] this applies when $X_0$ is in addition proper.
